{{2020–21 Mid-American Conference men's basketball standings}}

The '''2020–21 Ohio University Bobcats men's basketball team''' represented [[Ohio University]] for the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Bobcats were led by second-year head coach [[Jeff Boals]], who was a 1995 graduate of Ohio University.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/coaches/index|title=Men's Basketball|website=Ohio University|language=en|access-date=2019-10-16|archive-date=2019-10-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191016173856/https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/coaches/index|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/coaches/jeff-boals-1.html|title=Jeff Boals|website=Sports Reference|language=en|access-date=2022-09-29}}</ref> The team played their home games at the [[Convocation Center (Ohio University)|Convocation Center]] in [[Athens, Ohio]] as a member of the [[Mid-American Conference]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ohio.edu/building-directory/convocation-center|title=Convocation Center|website=Ohio University|language=en|access-date=2022-09-29}}</ref> In  a season limited due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], they finished the season 17–8, 9–5 in [[2020–21 Mid-American Conference men's basketball season|MAC play]] to finish in fifth place. As the No. 5 seed in the [[2021 MAC men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]], they defeated [[2020–21 Kent State Golden Flashes men's basketball team|Kent State]], [[2020–21 Toledo Rockets men's basketball team|Toledo]], and [[2020–21 Buffalo Bulls men's basketball team|Buffalo]] to win the tournament championship.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ohio Bobcats down Buffalo to win MAC Tournament, earn NCAA Tournament bid|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/ncaabk/ohio-bobcats-down-buffalo-to-win-mac-tournament-earn-ncaa-tournament-bid/ar-BB1eyNmz|website=Cincinnati Enquirer|language=en}}</ref> A a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 13 seed in the West region.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2020-21 Ohio Men's Basketball Schedule|url=https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/2020-21/schedule|access-date=2021-09-03|website=Ohio University|language=en}}</ref> There they upset No. 4-seeded [[2020–21 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] in the First Round<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ohio vs. Virginia - Game Recap - March 20, 2021 - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401310926|access-date=2021-10-25|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> before falling to No. 5-seeded [[2020–21 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]] in the Second Round.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ohio vs. Creighton - Game Recap - March 22, 2021 - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401310890|access-date=2021-10-25|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Henry|first=Megan|title=Athens celebrated March Madness game — despite outcome|url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/news/2021/03/22/ohio-university-athens-court-street-march-madness-creighton-game/4797106001/|access-date=2021-09-03|website=The Columbus Dispatch|language=en}}</ref>

==Previous season==

{{main|2019–20 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team}}

The [[2019–20 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team|Bobcats]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] 17–15, 8–10 in MAC play to finish in last place in the East division. As the No. 8 seed in the [[2020 MAC men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]], they defeated [[2019–20 Central Michigan Chippewas men's basketball team|Central Michigan]] in the first round before the tournament was canceled due to the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/2019-20/schedule|title=2019-20 Ohio Men's Basketball Schedule|website=Ohio University|language=en|access-date=2020-10-16|archive-date=2020-01-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200111203927/https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/2019-20/schedule|url-status=dead}}</ref>
